optional matching horizontal water-depth chord inside the far parabolic cross-section
optional semi-transparent water surface rectangle spanning the trough length between the two water-depth chords
cross-section model view with x-axis across trough width in inches
cross-section model view with y-axis showing depth upward from the vertex in inches

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The original 3D drawing is an extrusion of one parabolic end profile, and the given depth and top width determine the equation of that profile

interactions.label: Water overlay
interactions.teaches: The blue water surface is an added modeling layer, not part of the original diagram; when shown, its width comes from a horizontal chord of the parabola

interactions.label: Water depth h
interactions.teaches: As depth h increases, the horizontal chord of the parabola widens according to w(h)=2√(2h), so the water surface area changes with depth

demo_steps.title: Match the textbook diagram
demo_steps.narration: The default view shows only the black outline trough and the three given dimensions: 18 in deep, 3 ft long, and 12 in wide at the far top opening. No water surface or internal wireframe is shown.

demo_steps.title: Use the end dimensions
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the cross-section model. The vertex is at the bottom, and the top rim points are 6 in left and right of center at height 18 in, giving y = x²/2.

demo_steps.title: Add a water depth
demo_steps.narration: Turning on the water overlay draws a horizontal line y=h. Its intersections with the parabola give the water-surface width at that depth.

demo_steps.title: Relate the chord to surface area
demo_steps.narration: Back in the trough view, the same chord is extruded along the fixed 3 ft length. The surface area is width times length: A(h)=36·2√(2h) square inches.

plan.geometry_notes: Use inches as world units. Default trough dimensions are width 12 in, depth 18 in, length 36 in, so the bounding box is 12 × 18 × 36 world units. For the oblique coordinate convention: +X is screen-right across the trough opening, +Y is screen-up, and +Z is the receding trough length direction. The near cross-section lies in the X-Y plane at Z=0 and should appear at the left of the drawing. The far cross-section lies at Z=36 and should appear to the right and only slightly higher than the near end; project +Z mostly horizontally left-to-right, about 12–18 degrees upward, with oblique depth scale about 0.85–0.95 so the trough extends mostly horizontally like the source. Cross-section coordinates: vertex (0,0), top rim endpoints (-6,18) and (6,18), profile y = 0.5x^2 for x in [-6,6]. Draw the near U-shaped parabola from (-6,18,0) through (0,0,0) to (6,18,0). Draw the far U-shaped parabola from (-6,18,36) through (0,0,36) to (6,18,36). Draw only three longitudinal outline/generator lines: from (-6,18,0) to (-6,18,36), from (6,18,0) to (6,18,36), and from (0,0,0) to (0,0,36). Do not draw dense triangular mesh lines. The 18 in vertical dimension arrow is inside the near end, centered near x=0, from (0,18,0) down to (0,0,0), with the '18 in' label just to its left or right. The '3 ft' label sits parallel to and just above the upper front long rim line, roughly halfway between near and far ends. The 12 in width dimension belongs at the far end top opening: draw a short double-headed arrow from (-6,18,36) to (6,18,36), offset slightly upward in +Y if needed for readability, with '12 in' centered above it. Source palette is plain black-and-white: outlines, arrows, arrowheads, and text in #111111 on white #ffffff, no shading. Optional water overlay should be hidden by default; when enabled, use pale blue #4da3ff at opacity 0.25 for the surface and darker blue #1f77cc for the water chords. For water depth h, intersections satisfy 0.5x^2=h, so half-width is sqrt(2h), full width is w(h)=2sqrt(2h) inches, and fixed length is 36 inches, giving A(h)=36w(h)=72sqrt(2h) square inches.
plan.notes: Render the default trough as simple black THREE.Line curves and segments only, with consistent thin stroke weight and no filled side surfaces. Use a fixed oblique projection rather than an orbiting perspective camera so the diagram keeps the same left-to-right textbook composition. Keep all water geometry hidden when showWater is false, including blue surface, blue chords, and water labels. In cross-section model view, replace the 3D trough with a clean 2D plot of the same parabola and dimension-derived points; do not show both views simultaneously. Text labels should be screen-facing sprites or HTML overlays anchored to their dimension arrows.

authoredPrompt: This figure is a plain black-and-white line drawing of a trough in oblique three-dimensional view, with no shading or color. The body is a long open channel whose cross section is a parabola: the near end at the left is drawn as a U-shaped curve narrowing to a rounded point at the bottom, the same curve repeats at the far end on the right, and straight lines join the two rims along the length so the opening runs uniformly from end to end. Three measurements are marked. A double-headed vertical arrow inside the near end spans from the top rim down to the lowest point of the curve, labeled 18 in. A label along the upper front edge reads 3 ft for the length. A short segment across the far end of the top rim reads 12 in for the width across the opening. The flat rectangle formed by the rims and connecting lines represents the open water surface. Giving depth, length, and top width against a visible parabolic profile supplies just the quantities needed to fit an equation to the cross section and then write the water's surface area as a function of its depth.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for water depth: the learner raises and lowers a horizontal fill line inside the parabolic cross section and the water surface width changes, making clear that width is a function of depth rather than a constant.
- Toggle between 3D trough and cross-section graph: the learner switches from the channel view to the fitted parabola using 18 in depth and 12 in top width, making clear how the physical dimensions determine the equation for the end profile.
- Slider for trough length: the learner adjusts the 3 ft length and the water surface rectangle extends while the cross-section stays fixed, making clear how cross-sectional width and length combine to determine surface area.
- Equation input for the trough cross-section: learner edits a parabolic profile or the 18 in depth and 12 in width constraints; the cross-section and 3D trough fill redraw so width is derived from the entered curve.
authoredContext:
For example, suppose the Sustainability Club builds a water runoff collector in the shape of a parabolic trough as shown in the figure. We can use the information in the figure to find the surface area of the water in the trough as a function of the depth of the water.

Diagram of a parabolic trough that is 18” in height, 3’ in length, and 12” in width.

Because it will be helpful to have an equation for the parabolic cross-sectional shape, we will impose a coordinate system at the cross section, with x measured horizontally and y measured vertically, with the origin at the vertex of the parabola. See the figure.

interactions.label: Water depth h
interactions.teaches: The water surface width is not constant; it is the horizontal chord of the parabolic cross-section at depth h, so it grows as the water gets deeper

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The 3D trough is an extrusion of one parabolic end profile, and the 18 in depth plus 12 in top width determine the fitted cross-section equation

interactions.label: Trough length L
interactions.teaches: Changing the trough length stretches only the extrusion direction; the cross-section width at a given depth stays fixed, so surface area is width times length

interactions.label: Cross-section equation
interactions.teaches: The fill width is derived by intersecting the entered cross-section curve with the horizontal water-depth line, not by assigning a fixed width

demo_steps.title: Original trough dimensions
demo_steps.narration: The default 3D view matches the figure: a 3 ft long trough with a parabolic end that is 18 in deep and 12 in wide at the top. The water line is drawn as a horizontal chord inside the end profile.

demo_steps.title: See the fitted parabola
demo_steps.narration: Switching to the cross-section graph shows why the end profile is y = x²/2 when the vertex is at the bottom: the rim points are 6 in left and right of center at height 18 in.

demo_steps.title: Raise the water depth
demo_steps.narration: At a larger depth, the horizontal line cuts the parabola farther apart, so the water surface becomes wider. This makes the width a function of depth.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the trough
demo_steps.narration: Increasing the length extends the water surface rectangle down the channel while the cross-section chord width remains unchanged. Surface area combines these two quantities.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use inches as world units for the cross-section and convert length from feet to inches: default L = 3 ft = 36 in. Coordinate convention for the oblique drawing: +X is screen-right across the trough opening, +Y is screen-up, and +Z is the receding diagonal length direction running from the near left end toward the upper right. Near cross-section lies in the X-Y plane at Z=0; far cross-section lies at Z=12*L. Default trough bounding box is 12 × 18 × 36 world units: X from -6 to +6, Y from 0 to 18, Z from 0 to 36. The parabolic profile has vertex at (x,y)=(0,0) and top rim endpoints (-6,18) and (6,18), so y = (18/6^2)x^2 = 0.5x^2. For a water depth h, solve 0.5x^2 = h, giving half-width x = sqrt(2h), full water width w(h)=2sqrt(2h) inches for the default equation. Water surface area is A(h,L)=w(h)*(12L) square inches. In 3D view, draw the near U-shaped parabola at Z=0 on the left, the far U-shaped parabola at Z=12L to the right/up along the oblique receding direction, upper rim lines from (-6,18,0) to (-6,18,12L) and from (6,18,0) to (6,18,12L), and the bottom line from (0,0,0) to (0,0,12L). The 18 in arrow is vertical inside the near end, slightly left of center, from y=18 down to y=0. The 3 ft label sits along the upper long rim edge. The 12 in label sits above the far top chord from x=-6 to x=6 at y=18. Source palette is black line art on white: outlines #111111, labels #111111, dimension arrows #111111. Add water as translucent pale blue #4da3ff with opacity about 0.28, using a darker blue #1f77cc for the fill chord.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the source-like trough primarily as thin black curves and line segments, with no heavy shading. Use an oblique projection transform so the cross-section appears nearly true while the length recedes diagonally up and right. For equation input, sample y(x) over the supplied domain and find the two outer intersections with y=h to place the water chord; if there are not two valid intersections, show an inline parse/domain warning and hide the water surface rather than inventing a width. Keep the dimension labels anchored to the default physical dimensions even when the learner edits the equation, but let the curve, intersection chord, and water surface redraw from the current parsed profile.

discrepancies: The far/right end is drawn as a full, prominent parabolic cross-section, whereas the source shows the far end mostly as a partial outer curved edge with stronger occlusion by the trough body.
The generated trough appears as an open wireframe skeleton with both end parabolas equally explicit, while the source emphasizes a continuous trough outline with fewer visible interior/end edges.
The 12 in dimension is shown as a separate bracket above the far opening rather than integrated with the short far top-width edge as in the source.
The overall oblique projection and proportions make the right end appear too tall/prominent relative to the left end compared with the source.
The generated figure includes extra interactive controls, readouts, optional water/graph modes, and equation content that are not part of the original static textbook figure.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is recognizably the same parabolic trough with correct main dimensions, but the far-end visibility, wireframe emphasis, and added teaching controls make it less faithful to the sparse source drawing.
action_items: Reduce or hide the back-side portions of the far parabolic end so it resembles the partially visible right curved edge in the source.
Adjust the oblique camera/projection so the far end is not visually larger or more dominant than the near end.
Make the 12 in dimension look more like the source by aligning it with the far top-width edge rather than using a large standalone bracket.
For the default view, keep only the three source dimension labels and black outline geometry visually dominant.

feedback.rationale: The concept and plan are correct, but the critic identifies generator-level faithfulness issues—far-end visibility, camera/proportion, dimension placement, and extra hallucinated controls—that can be fixed in rendering.
